member.name: T:Lumio.Engine.NativeLoader.NativeHfsmDefinition
member.summary: A compiled HFSM definition living in native memory.

remarks.para: This is the managed door to NativeCore lumio-hfsm, the engine's only transition semantics implementation (ADR-069 rule 1, R-00571). The kernel computes the transition; this class does not. Nothing here walks the state graph, resolves priorities or decides what to exit and enter — it marshals PODs across the ABI and marshals the plan back.

The division of labour is fixed: the host holds the , answers guards up front (native never calls back into managed code — ADR-006), and executes the actions the plan names. Writing a second transition table in C# is exactly what this type exists to stop.

Cost: every Start / Send / Stop allocates the output buffers (sized from / ), pins four arrays and makes three unmanaged allocations; the native side adds its own scratch. This is not a zero-cost call. A caller stepping many machines per tick — a GAS ability machine per entity, say — should measure before putting it on the hot path; batching several machines into one crossing is a known follow-up, not something this shape gives for free today.

member.name: T:Lumio.Engine.NativeLoader.INativeHfsmAbi
member.summary: The four native hfsm_* root slots behind an interface, so the managed facade's own marshalling can be tested without loading a native artifact — the same seam INativeTimerAbi, INativeLogAbi and INativeClockAbi use (those three stay in Lumio.Engine.NativeLoader, which references this assembly, so they cannot be cref-linked from here).

remarks.para: This is a Context-bound projection of native handles and caller-owned buffers, not the shape gameplay code should use. Consumers go through .

It is public because implementing it is the supported way to drive the facade without a native artifact (R-00578): a consumer's own test double, and the wasm32 path, which cannot go through Marshal.GetDelegateForFunctionPointer over the root table at all. Implementing this interface does not make a second transition table legal — the semantics still come from lumio-hfsm alone (ADR-069 rule 1).
